sections.h2: Which office bills and which one values?
sections.html:
Two offices on Marietta Highway in Canton share the work. The Tax Commissioner bills real estate, personal property, public utility, timber, motor vehicle and mobile home taxes, then sends the collections to the state, county, school and city governments. The Tax Assessors' Office decides what your property is worth and which exemptions you get.

  • Tax Commissioner: 678-493-6400, cherokeecountytax.com. The main office is at 2780 Marietta Hwy, Canton, with an annex at 155 Towne Lake Pkwy, Woodstock. Both are open 8:00am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Tax Assessors' Office: 678-493-6120, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton. Returns are filed here until the season ends April 1.
  • City tax offices bill separately inside Ball Ground, Canton, Holly Springs, Mountain Park, Nelson, Waleska and Woodstock, so find out whether your address is incorporated.

The Assessors' Office posts a public notice that appraisal staff may visit after an appeal, a new return, new construction or a conservation use application. Visitors carry county photo identification and drive marked county vehicles, and answering their questions is voluntary.

Cherokee has 434 square miles, of which 422 are land. Interstate 575 runs through the middle from Kennesaw by way of Woodstock, Holly Springs and Canton to Ball Ground, and the southern end nearest Atlanta is the most densely settled. One school district, the Cherokee County School District, serves every address.

Population reached 299,273 in 2025, 12.2% above the 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-held house is worth $435,100, median household income is $108,115 and 77.3% of homes are owner-occupied. Builders pulled 1,524 permits in 2025.

Cherokee mails bills in September and wants payment by November 15. A balance left after that date is delinquent, and the Tax Commissioner notes that a lien then attaches to the property. Mobile home bills arrive each January and are due April 1.

One mill equals a dollar for each thousand dollars of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of market value in Georgia. The county's rates for 2026 and 2025 are below.

The fire levy explains why bills differ between a Canton address and an unincorporated one such as Hickory Flat or Lake Arrowhead. A city may add its own levy on top of these county figures.

Write out your appeal and get it to the assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice went in the mail. The state's uniform form asks you to choose a Board of Equalization hearing, a hearing officer or arbitration. The grounds may be taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

County appraisal staff value property with sales comparison, cost and income approaches and test the results statistically by area, neighborhood and class of property. A good appeal answers those methods with your own evidence.

  • Recent closed sales of similar houses nearby, with dates and prices.
  • Photos and repair estimates that show condition problems the record may not reflect.
  • A copy of your settlement statement or warranty deed if you bought the property recently.

Complaints about the size of the tax fall outside an appeal, because assessors do not set millage rates. The governing bodies named on your bill do that.

Apply in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, carrying a valid Georgia driver's license or ID that shows the property's address. Take your settlement statement or warranty deed too, because staff print and complete the application on the spot.

The state's standard homestead exemption covers an owner-occupied primary residence, and the county can add to it. Applications are taken all year but must be in by April 1 to count for that tax year, and skipping the application waives the exemption. Ask the office which Cherokee County exemptions for seniors, disabled service members or surviving spouses fit your situation, since the amounts change.

An exemption follows the person who applied, so a buyer starts over with a new application.

sections.h2: What selling does to the tax bill
sections.html:
Title on New Year's Day decides who is taxed, and the Tax Commissioner has no legal way to prorate a part year. If you and the buyer want a split, you must agree on it at closing.

A buyer who closes in the fall will not automatically get a bill. The Tax Commissioner asks for the closing statement so the bill can be reissued in the new owner's name, which works for purchases completed before November 15 of that tax year. If October 1 passes with no bill in hand, phone 678-493-6400 or print one from the website. Even when the bill stays in the seller's name, the lien follows the property if it turns delinquent.

A properly completed PT-61 transfer form on file at the Superior Court clerk's office can stand in for a new real property return in the sale year, as long as nothing was subdivided or built.

sections.h2: When property goes to tax sale
sections.html:
The winning bidder at a tax sale receives a tax deed but cannot take possession, build, or evict tenants straight away. For 12 months the owner, a lender or anyone else with an interest may buy the property back.

The redemption price is the bid, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward, plus special assessments, plus a premium of 20% of the amount for the first year or part of a year and 10% for each year after that, plus sheriff and advertising costs. After 12 months the buyer may serve a notice of foreclosure of the right to redeem by certified mail to the recorded owner and each interest holder, and the notice must also be printed weekly for four straight weeks in the county newspaper.

If an auction brings in more than is owed, the surplus is held separately. O.C.G.A. 48-4-5 lets the owner of record at that time, plus security deed holders, claim it. Claimants are not required to pay or hire anyone to get it.

Print your bill at cherokeecountytax.com or call 678-493-6400 to learn the balance, and ask if any earlier year is open. Send the closing statement to the Tax Commissioner after you close so the next bill goes to the right name. Tell the buyer to apply for their own homestead exemption at the Assessors' Office before April 1.

If the house sits inside one of the seven cities, ask that city's tax office for its balance too. A cash sale follows the same steps, and because it can close sooner, request your figures early.

faqs.q: When must a Cherokee County bill be paid?
faqs.a: November 15. Bills are mailed in September, and taxes not paid by that date are considered delinquent.

faqs.q: Will the Cherokee County Tax Commissioner prorate at a sale?
faqs.a: No. The office has no legal provision for prorating partial-year ownership, so any split is settled by the parties at closing.

faqs.q: Where can I file for homestead in Cherokee County?
faqs.a: File in person at the Tax Assessors' Office, 2782 Marietta Hwy, Suite 200, Canton, with a Georgia license or ID showing the property address.

faqs.q: How long can an owner redeem after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Twelve months from the sale date. After that the buyer may start the foreclosure of the right to redeem by sending notice.

faqs.q: How can I find my Cherokee County tax bill if I did not receive one?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Commissioner at 678-493-6400 or print a copy from cherokeecountytax.com. The office suggests doing so if a bill has not arrived by October 1.
